evidence:
The authoritative workbook Quality Checks!A20:D20 requires installation to expected paths and operation under the stated contract. Its internal row still says no network/runtime install; the public-network correction in the authoritative row and skill takes precedence.

Frozen task source: solution/solve.sh:1-34 is LF-only (34 LF, zero CRLF), begins #!/bin/bash, copies its co-located app into /app (line 33), bounds its fresh-install database deletion to /app (lines 5-9,34), and writes nothing into /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution. It contains no pkill or NODE_ENV=production. The actual successful bash execution supports syntax validity. solution/app/server.js:2 loads src/index.js, whose main thread starts bootstrap and worker remains in the same Node process. src/bootstrap.js:20-23 returns health without touching the database; lines 43-45 bind 0.0.0.0 using PORT or 3000. src/db.js:13,22-28 honors DB_PATH; lines 122-124 skip seeding a populated database. The co-located seed hash exactly equals environment/assets/seed_data.json (1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7). Only Node built-ins, Express and better-sqlite3 are required; the frozen Dockerfile preinstalls those versions through NODE_PATH.

Measured evidence: local/install-lifecycle.py:start() starts env -i with the stated NODE_PATH, PORT=3000, DB_PATH=/app/app.db and uid/gid 65534, runs node /app/server.js from /tests, and checks installed bytes. install-lifecycle/results.json records fresh solve exit 0, authenticated creation, preserved saved record after actual MCP replacement PID 21 -> 97, and closed reinstall returning exactly 7 requisitions/13 offers. The initial driver attempt expected a specific in-use message; actual active reinstall exited 1 on /proc EACCES before copying/deleting, and the corrected driver verified the saved record remained intact. This establishes safe refusal, not successful identification of an open SQLite handle. local/domain/results.json additionally records exact business-state retention without reseeding on a replacement process; scripts/check_hireops_domain.cjs:21 uses the alternate output/domain.sqlite DB_PATH.

Hashes were recomputed: lifecycle results 613da9cf8e275402f708957981b3cefe2236d55803f7b9efaaee7618e1ff15a8; lifecycle driver 05780ac5eb6f1e441ef5a946a36f466ad7cdee7ae239b5f7d7d9f5933f39e024; successful attempt log f7f266fbbe665755ffda123c2101298d103ae99f74c4fb470f5480391721f093; solve.sh 3bf863a5703a9c7297986ca72a6300b47780546531e966b3a7386982dc852741. The indexed 35 source hashes for lifecycle and domain evidence all match frozen bytes, as do all 11 recorded solution-app hashes and relevant raw artifact hashes. Domain driver hash 80b278db3f020c944c4e46903e851bf0ce5e97216d2c948cbacc1954f70bb3b9 also matches. Shared launch script and Dockerfile equal the frozen template by SHA256.

Counterexample reasoning: a health-only fake or memory-only app could fool liveness but cannot satisfy the measured authenticated creation and exact saved-record readback after process replacement. A conforming app using file-relative paths, another working directory, an alternate DB_PATH, or permitted browser CDN assets must remain acceptable; the first three are supported here by source and measured launches, and no offline-network requirement was imposed. This narrow Pass covers the reference runtime contract; it does not claim a private deterministic checker execution, configured judge score, Oracle score or portal clearance.
